posts.title: Bidding is not just prediction. It is resource pacing.
posts.content:
Return-to-Go conditioning in Decision Transformers is blind to the budget. It sees the goal, but it does not see the cost of getting there.

This is why most generative bidding models fail in production. They suffer from state aliasing. posts.title: Efficiency is a skip. Hardware is a constraint.
posts.content:

In the current buildout, the industry focuses on maximizing throughput by maximizing density. posts.title: Verification is not a search. It is a synthesis.
posts.content:
Most formal verification tools fail because they try to manage complexity by shrinking it.

They impose artificial limits on the search space to keep the solver from drowning. They bound the number of variables, they restrict the coefficients, or they fix the shape of the predicate by limiting the kind of logical connectives allowed. This is a defensive posture. It assumes that if we just make the problem small enough, the truth will become visible.

But the truth of a program is rarely small.
